title: K8s → EKS Fargate Migration
description: Migrate workloads from on-premises Kubernetes cluster to Amazon EKS with AWS Fargate for serverless compute.

steps.action: Create EKS cluster with eksctl: eksctl create cluster --name analytics-eks --fargate --region us-east-1 --version 1.31 --vpc-nat-mode HighlyAvailable
steps.verify: kubectl get nodes shows Fargate virtual nodes; kubectl cluster-info returns EKS API endpoint

steps.action: Create Fargate profiles for each namespace: eksctl create fargateprofile --cluster analytics-eks --name fp-analytics --namespace analytics
steps.verify: aws eks describe-fargate-profile shows ACTIVE status for each namespace

steps.action: Migrate Kubernetes manifests: replace resource requests/limits for Fargate vCPU/memory combos; remove hostPath volumes (use EFS CSI driver instead); update RBAC to use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA)
steps.verify: kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifests/ shows 0 validation errors

steps.action: Install EFS CSI driver: helm install aws-efs-csi-driver aws-efs-csi-driver/aws-efs-csi-driver; create PersistentVolume claims pointing to EFS file system
steps.verify: kubectl get pvc -A shows all Bound; pods mount EFS volumes successfully
steps.rollback: Uninstall EFS CSI driver; revert PVC to NFS or EBS

steps.action: Deploy workloads to EKS: kubectl apply -f manifests/ —namespace analytics; validate pod startup and liveness probes
steps.verify: kubectl get pods -n analytics shows all Running; application health checks pass
steps.rollback: kubectl delete -f manifests/; re-run on source K8s cluster
